head: claude/mi63-true-blocked-on-edges
title: work store: record the assessments already made, write 3 true edges, and grade how a stage was arrived at (MI-63)
body:
## What this is

MI-63. The constraint readout refuses (`insufficient_basis`) and two build phases are held by that refusal. This does **not** raise coverage to clear the floor. It establishes what was actually there, adds the small number of edges that are **true**, and fixes the reason the diagnosis could never have worked anyway.

**Population for every number below:** every `*.yaml` in `docs/claude/work/objects/`, n=584 before this change, **0 parse failures**.

## 1 — The 6-vs-2 discrepancy is explained, and the readout is NOT wrong

`constraint_readout.py` counts a row with **any** typed edge as assessed — writing an edge *is* a positive statement — while the `blocked_on_basis` **field** was simply absent on 4 of the 6. Neither number was wrong; they answer different questions. Measured: `blocked` 6 · `declared_none` 0 · `unstated` 578, against a field census of `ASSESSED` 2 · `NOT_ASSESSED` 576 · `<missing>` 6.

Added `blocked_on_basis` to `WO-20260901-PHASE-{A,B,C,H}` — **recording an assessment that was already made, not creating one**. Coverage is unchanged at 1.03%; field and code now agree at 6. The 2 rows still without a basis (PHASE-E/F) carry no edges and correctly grade `unstated`.

## 2 — The stage histogram is a census of FILENAMES (the bigger half)

**576 of 584 objects' `stage` is a deterministic function of one field.** `migrate_backlog_to_work_objects.py::SOURCES` maps `health-review-backlog.json` → INTEGRITY (498) and `{ml,performance,research}-review-backlog.json` → EVIDENCE (78), with **no per-row judgement and zero exceptions**; the other 8 are the build's own phases, all CAPABILITY. So `INTEGRITY 498` counts one filename, and **not one object in the store had its chain stage chosen by someone reading the work.**

QUESTION / DECISION / DEPLOYMENT / OBSERVATION are therefore empty **by construction** — no producer has ever emitted one. `operating-model-DESIGN.md` names **DECISION** as the measured constraint, so the store cannot locate the stage the design says the system is stuck on, **at any edge coverage**.

⚠️ **This is independent of the coverage problem, and that is the point.** Assessing all 584 objects with perfectly true edges would leave DECISION at whatever anyone hand-authored — the readout would clear its floor and then name a stage **confidently**, off a histogram describing four backlog filenames. The refusal is currently the only thing stopping that.

Remedied by grading **`stage_basis`** (`per_object` · `bulk_by_source_file` · `unstated`, never collapsed, summing to the population checkably, derived from the row's own `source` block rather than asserted), surfaced in `READOUT.md` and the `CLAUDE.md` brief. Six new self-test cases.

**The chain work exists — it is outside the store under a different vocabulary.** `OPEN-ITEMS.json` holds `pending_decision` 3 (= DECISION) and `monitoring` 21 + `awaiting_verification` 6 (= OBSERVATION). Phase C carried the review **backlogs** and never the **register**.

## 3 — Three true edges, from rows whose own `clears_when` establishes the blocker

| new object | stage | edge | why it is true, not invented |
|---|---|---|---|
| `WO-20260902-DECISION-REVIEW-PACKET-POPULATION` | DECISION | `operator_decision` | Source row's `clears_when` says the operator must record a decision on § 4A and **names both alternatives**. No session can settle it by working. |
| `WO-20260902-DECISION-LOCAL-LLM-WEIGHT` | DECISION | `operator_decision` | Its `clears_when` ends with the literal sentence *"Then the operator decides"*; both size arms are benchmarked. |
| `WO-20260902-EVIDENCE-TRADE-PRIORITISATION-AB` | EVIDENCE | `capability` | See below. |

**The third one is the one I want reviewed.** It is filed upstream as `kind: pending_decision`, and it is deliberately **not** staged DECISION. Its own text says the A/B *"CANNOT BE RUN TODAY"* because `backtest_system.py` models one shared book — so what is held up is EVIDENCE, and what holds it is a missing CAPABILITY. Staging it DECISION was the easy way to take DECISION from 0 to 3, and it would have put a question on the operator **they cannot answer** — a false blocker, which is worse than a missing one. It is also a worked example of the E2 pull rule: a named stage held up by a named missing capability.

Each new object states what is **not** claimed. The trade-prioritisation edge records that I did **not** read `backtest_system.py` to confirm the single-book claim — it is carried as the source session's measurement, not re-verified as mine.

## What is deliberately NOT done

**No bulk annotation of the 578 `NOT_ASSESSED` rows.** The verdict still reads `insufficient_basis` at **1.53% (9/587)** and that remains the correct output.

## Validation

- `scripts/ci/run_guards.py`: **PASS 51 · FAIL 0** (`layer-guard` needed `import-linter` installed; `lint-imports` then reports 6 kept / 0 broken).
- `constraint_readout.py --self-test`: ALL PASS, incl. 6 new `stage_basis` cases.
- `pytest` over the artifact-validity + operator-owed sets: 111 passed.
- Two guards caught real defects in my own first draft and are fixed here: a **truncated backlog id in prose** that resolved to nothing, and an **unstated percentage**. Both were correct catches.
- `OPEN-ITEMS.json` was **not** touched (per `BL-20260902-OPEN-ITEMS-IS-THE-ONE-REGISTER-NO-APPEND-HELPER-PROTECTS`); the backlog row went through `backlog_append.py::append_row` (19 lines added, 0 removed).

## One thing found in passing, for whoever owns it

`DEC-20260901-READ-GATE-SEQUENCING` on `WO-20260901-PHASE-H` **has been answered and committed** (`accept_ungated`, 2026-09-02, `answered_by: telegram`). That is a real end-to-end decision round-trip. It does **not** clear `OI-20260901-DECISION-ROUNDTRIP-...`, whose `clears_when` requires an answer *submitted from the deployed SPA* — this came via Telegram. Reported rather than edited, to avoid colliding on `OPEN-ITEMS.json` with whoever built that channel.
